=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2525 and the parallel V1 path at 2576 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: State-auth verification passes the candidate state's own integration_branch as the verification context, making the branch binding check self-referential.
  WHY: The removed canonical-equality check previously rejected signed-but-wrong-branch state; HMAC forgery is infeasible, but poller-signed unexpected-branch state can now drive syncs, merges, and resolver dispatches instead of pausing. Qwen/qwen3_7-plus disagreed that this remains an unfixed defect because custom integration branches were deliberately supported.
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:157-158 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: `_validated_auth_context()` replaces the canonical `integration_branch != f"orchestrator/project-{tracking_issue}"` check with `STATE_AUTH_BRANCH_RE.fullmatch(integration_branch) is None`, enabling the same self-verification pattern.
  WHY: Combined with the shell-side forwarding of the candidate branch as the verification context, verification no longer compares the signed branch against the expected value; the HMAC still binds the branch, but the canonical branch defense-in-depth check is gone. Qwen/qwen3_7-plus disagreed that this remains an unfixed defect because custom integration branches were deliberately supported.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8162-8170 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: A retryable judge failure preserves `unresolved_ticks` unchanged and increments `integration_conflict_total_dispatches`, so the next poll tick re-invokes the full Codex judge without a cooldown.
  WHY: A persistent judge-side failure consumes one unit of the `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX=10` budget every poll tick and can terminalize a project in roughly 50 minutes, converting a transient provider outage into project failure.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:26-27 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Declaring `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_AUTH_KEYRING: required: true` means every consumer repo must provision the secret before the next `@stable` promotion or its reusable poller workflow fails at queue time.
  WHY: The workflow never reaches the in-script `validate-keyring` gate or sends an in-run alert, while the changelog and README.md:61 do not document the mandatory per-consumer provisioning step or the resulting failure mode.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 2525 and the parallel V1 path at 2576
  Problem: State-auth verification passes the candidate state's own integration_branch as the verification context, making the branch binding check tautological.
  Why it fails at runtime: HMAC forgery is infeasible without the key, so an external attacker cannot exploit this. The practical risk is when a bug in the poller's state-signing path produces state with a non-canonical branch — the old code rejected this and paused; the new code accepts it and drives syncs, merges, and resolver dispatches against a branch that was not the expected one for the project.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py
  Line or code reference: 157-158
  Problem: `_validated_auth_context()` replaces the canonical `integration_branch != f"orchestrator/project-{tracking_issue}"` check with `STATE_AUTH_BRANCH_RE.fullmatch(integration_branch) is None`. This is the Python-side counterpart of the shell finding above and enables the same self-verification pattern.
  Why it fails at runtime: Combined with the shell-side forwarding of the candidate branch as the verification context, this removes the defense-in-depth check that a validly signed state matches the tracking issue's canonical branch. The HMAC still binds the branch in the signature, but verification no longer compares that bound branch against the expected value.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 2525 (`candidate_verification_branch="${candidate_integration_branch:-${expected_integration_branch}}"` passed as `--integration-branch` to `orchestrate_state_v2.py verify`), the parallel V1 block at 2576, and the companion relaxation in scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:157-158 (canonical-equality check replaced by `STATE_AUTH_BRANCH_RE.fullmatch`)
  Problem: State-auth verification is now self-referential for the integration branch: the branch string embedded in the candidate payload is used as the verification context, so `state_document.integration_branch in ("", ctx)` (orchestrate_state_v2.py:385) and the field-equality check at :398 compare the payload against itself.
  Why it fails at runtime: No forgery path exists; the failure mode is loss of the fail-closed property against poller-signed-but-unexpected-branch state, plus a docs-vs-code contradiction on a security invariant.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 8162-8170 (the `_integration_judge_rc -eq 2` branch in `heal_integration_branch_conflict`)
  Problem: A retryable judge failure preserves `unresolved_ticks` unchanged and increments `integration_conflict_total_dispatches` by one. Because `unresolved_ticks` stays >= `effective_max_retries`, the very next poll tick re-invokes the full Codex judge with no cooldown.
  Why it fails at runtime: A persistent judge-side failure consumes one unit of the `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX=10` budget every poll tick, terminalizing a project as `status=failed` in roughly 50 minutes.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml
  Line or code reference: 26-27 (`ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_AUTH_KEYRING: required: true` under `workflow_call.secrets`)
  Problem: Declaring the brand-new secret `required: true` on the reusable poller workflow means every consumer repo must provision `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_AUTH_KEYRING` before the next `@stable` promotion, or its synced `ai-orchestrate-poll.yml` cron wrapper starts failing at queue time on every 5-minute tick.
  Why it fails at runtime: GitHub rejects the reusable-workflow call for a missing required secret; no step runs, so no in-run Telegram alert fires, and consumer orchestrator polling hard-fails repo-wide until each consumer manually adds the secret.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
